rationale_evidence.anchor: Adequate \land \neg C(R) \Rightarrow not realizable, though the information is present. ... This is why C belongs in the frame and not in the transformation.

(anchor: "Zero is not sufficiency -- adequacy is. ... Sufficiency is about what a representation retains. Zero is about what a case can lose.")

(anchor: "Zero fails in both directions between the element level and the set level. It is therefore not an irrelevance relation in the graphoid sense ... [x,x] ... redundancy ... [+c,-c] ... emergent eliminability")
- [S2738] types=[EXPERIMENTAL-RESULT] scope=OBJECT — "States the Remainder trichotomy's exact positive identity: 'not eliminated' equals exactly 'contract-relevant unresolved material' without exception in 1182/1182 tested cases, while the transformation residual (B) is a genuinely different object, separating the residue of the operation from the residue of the concern." (anchor: "A - Eliminated \equiv C in 1182/1182 -- exactly ... B is a different object. The transformation residual is not what the contract leaves unresolved.")
- [S2738] types=[EXPERIMENTAL-RESULT, WARNING] scope=OBJECT — "Reports the asymmetric-bias finding as a concept-level warning: a rule-over-field-types eliminability heuristic is wrong far more often in the dangerous over-elimination direction than the safe direction, so eliminability must never be implemented as such a rule." (anchor: "One elimination in six is blocked by boundary information alone ... the rule-based and counterfactual notions of eliminability agree only 55.75% of the time ... 1559 elements the rule would remove are not Zero, against 301 that are Zero but the rule keeps.")
- [S2738] types=[EXPERIMENTAL-RESULT, CORRECTION] scope=OBJECT — "Establishes that repeated-elimination L is reductive, terminating and iteration-monotone-decreasing but non-confluent (11/1162 non-commuting) and only operator-relative idempotent; concludes 'eliminate everything eliminable' names no unique object unless an order is fixed and declared." (anchor: "L is not a projection and not an interior operator. It is a terminating, non-confluent rewriting process. ... Which normal form you reach depends on the order you eliminate in.")
- [S2738] types=[OPEN-QUESTION] scope=OBJECT — "Names the deepest unresolved question about the Zero concept: no replacement group/set formulation exists even though the element-wise one is refuted in both directions; also leaves L's monotonicity, k>3 higher-order eliminability, and semantic equivalence explicitly open." (anchor: "Is there a well-defined group/set formulation of Zero? OPEN -- H5+H6 show the element-wise formulation fails in both directions; they do not supply the replacement. This is the deepest open question about the concept.")

(anchor: "A representation R=T(D) realizes Q under decoder O iff O(R)=Q(D). ... O is fixed in advance, as part of the inquiry frame. ... - [S2739] types=[ARGUMENT, DISTINCTION] scope=OBJECT — "Distinguishes Adequacy (does R determine Q, an existential/population-level question) from Realization (does this fixed decoder recover Q, a per-case question), showing they diverge for two independent reasons: a weaker-than-needed decoder, or a failing use-time constraint C." (anchor: "Adequate \land \neg C(R) \Rightarrow not realizable, though the information is present. ... This is why C belongs in the frame and not in the transformation.")
- [S2739] types=[LIMITATION, EXPERIMENTAL-RESULT] scope=OBJECT — "Names a specific design defect: the chain's transformations never dropped a record so C could never fail, and the decoder was strong enough at the one adequate level, so the experiment excluded its own target case by construction -- the separation is real by definition but was never exhibited." - [S2739] types=[HYPOTHESIS] scope=OBJECT — "States the one open conjecture in the document with an explicit refutation condition (a decoder right by luck on observed cases without being determined by R), noting the converse (Adequacy=>Realization) is already refuted."
